fresco = a painting done on wet plaster, usually on a wall or ceiling
mural = a large painting on a wall, often in a public place
collage = art made by sticking different materials onto a surface
installation art = a three-dimensional artwork designed for a particular space
contemporary art = art being made in the present period
street art = art in public spaces, including murals and stencils, often unsanctioned
graffiti = writing or drawings, often sprayed, on walls in public places
pop art = mid-twentieth-century art that uses images from advertising and mass culture
canvas = a strong cloth surface on which oil paintings are usually made
palette = the board on which an artist mixes colours; the range of colours used
composition = the way shapes, colours and figures are arranged in a work of art
perspective = the technique of drawing objects so they appear to recede in space
self-portrait = a picture an artist makes of themselves
art collector = a person who buys artworks, often as an investment or passion
forgery = a fake artwork made to look like the work of a famous artist
restoration = repairing and cleaning an artwork or historic object
broadsheet = a serious newspaper, traditionally printed on large sheets
tabloid = a popular newspaper with short articles, big headlines and many photos
bias = an unfair preference for or against a person, group or idea
breaking news = news that is just coming in and is being reported immediately
